\chapter{Communication Complexity --- Entropy}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.NewmanTheorem.Entropy
\section{Overview}

This module collects entropy and mutual-information lemmas needed for the Newman theorem
development.  It establishes upper bounds on (Shannon) entropy in terms of alphabet size,
monotonicity and data-processing inequalities for mutual information and conditional mutual
information, chain rules, and stability results under almost-sure equality and identical
distributions.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Entropy bounded by log of alphabet size]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.entropy_le_log_of_card_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
If the alphabet type $S$ has $\mathrm{card}(S) \le N$, then for any random variable
$X : \Omega \to S$ and measure $\mu$,
\[
  H[X;\mu] \;\le\; \log N.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Entropy bounded by $c \log 2$ when alphabet fits in $c$ bits]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.entropy_le_nat_mul_log_two_of_card_le_two_pow}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.entropy_le_log_of_card_le}
\difficulty{2}
If $\mathrm{card}(S) \le 2^c$ for some $c : \mathbb{N}$, then
\[
  H[X;\mu] \;\le\; c \cdot \log 2.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mutual information bounded by left entropy]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.mutualInfo_le_entropy_left}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For measurable $X$ and $Y$ under a zero-or-probability measure $\mu$ with finite ranges,
\[
  I[X : Y;\mu] \;\le\; H[X;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mutual information bounded by right entropy]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.mutualInfo_le_entropy_right}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.mutualInfo_le_entropy_left}
\difficulty{2}
For measurable $X$ and $Y$ under a zero-or-probability measure $\mu$ with finite ranges,
\[
  I[X : Y;\mu] \;\le\; H[Y;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mutual information invariant under a.e.\ substitution]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.mutualInfo_congr_ae}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
If $X =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} X'$ and $Y =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} Y'$, then
$I[X : Y;\mu] = I[X' : Y';\mu]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mutual information invariant under injective recoding of right variable]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.mutualInfo_comp_right_of_injective}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
If $f : T \to V$ is measurable and injective, then
$I[X : f \circ Y;\mu] = I[X : Y;\mu]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mutual information zero when left variable is a.e.\ constant]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_const_left}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
If $X =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} c$ for some constant $c : S$, then $I[X : Y;\mu] = 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mutual information zero when right variable is a.e.\ constant]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_const_right}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_const_left}
\difficulty{2}
If $Y =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} c$ for some constant $c : T$, then $I[X : Y;\mu] = 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional mutual information zero when left variable is a.e.\ constant]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_const_left}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
If $X =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} c$ for some constant $c : S$, then $I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] = 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional mutual information zero when right variable is a.e.\ constant]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_const_right}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_const_left}
\difficulty{2}
If $Y =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} c$ for some constant $c : T$, then $I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] = 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Independence from singleton-fiber factorization]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.indepFun_of_measureReal_inter_preimage_singleton_eq_mul}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
For measurable $X : \Omega \to S$ and $Y : \Omega \to T$ with finite $S$ and $T$, if
\[
  \mu(X^{-1}\{x\} \cap Y^{-1}\{y\}) = \mu(X^{-1}\{x\})\cdot\mu(Y^{-1}\{y\})
\]
holds for all $x, y$, then $X$ and $Y$ are independent under $\mu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional mutual information bounded by left conditional entropy]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_le_condEntropy_left}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For measurable $X$, $Y$, $Z$ under a zero-or-probability measure with finite ranges,
\[
  I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] \;\le\; H[X \mid Z;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional mutual information bounded by right conditional entropy]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_le_condEntropy_right}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_le_condEntropy_left}
\difficulty{2}
For measurable $X$, $Y$, $Z$ under a zero-or-probability measure with finite ranges,
\[
  I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] \;\le\; H[Y \mid Z;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional mutual information bounded by left entropy]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_le_entropy_left}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_le_condEntropy_left}
\difficulty{2}
For measurable $X$, $Y$, $Z$ under a zero-or-probability measure with finite ranges,
\[
  I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] \;\le\; H[X;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional mutual information bounded by right entropy]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_le_entropy_right}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_le_condEntropy_right}
\difficulty{2}
For measurable $X$, $Y$, $Z$ under a zero-or-probability measure with finite ranges,
\[
  I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] \;\le\; H[Y;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional data processing: postprocessing depending on conditioning value]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_comp_left_le_of_comp_conditioning}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
If $f : U \to S \to V$ is any function (where $Z : \Omega \to U$ is the conditioning
variable), then applying $f(Z(\omega))$ to $X(\omega)$ before measuring mutual information
cannot increase it:
\[
  I[\omega \mapsto f(Z(\omega))(X(\omega)) : Y \mid Z;\mu]
  \;\le\; I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional data processing on the right depending on conditioning value]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_comp_right_le_of_comp_conditioning}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_comp_left_le_of_comp_conditioning}
\difficulty{3}
For a measurable function $f : U \to T \to V$ (with $Z : \Omega \to U$ the conditioning
variable), applying $f(Z(\omega))$ to $Y(\omega)$ cannot increase conditional mutual information:
\[
  I[X : \omega \mapsto f(Z(\omega))(Y(\omega)) \mid Z;\mu]
  \;\le\; I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditioning on $(Z, f(Z))$ equals conditioning on $Z$]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_conditioning_prod_function_eq}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
Adding a deterministic function of the conditioning variable to the conditioning variable does
not change conditional mutual information:
\[
  I[X : Y \mid (\omega \mapsto (Z(\omega),\, f(Z(\omega))));\mu]
  \;=\; I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Extra left-side conditioning cannot increase conditional mutual information]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_conditioning_prod_left_function_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
For a measurable $f : U \to S \to V$, conditioning additionally on a deterministic function
of $X$ and $Z$ cannot increase conditional mutual information:
\[
  I[X : Y \mid (\omega \mapsto (Z(\omega),\, f(Z(\omega))(X(\omega))));\mu]
  \;\le\; I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Extra right-side conditioning cannot increase conditional mutual information]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_conditioning_prod_right_function_le}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_conditioning_prod_left_function_le}
\difficulty{2}
For a measurable $f : U \to T \to V$, conditioning additionally on a deterministic function
of $Y$ and $Z$ cannot increase conditional mutual information:
\[
  I[X : Y \mid (\omega \mapsto (Z(\omega),\, f(Z(\omega))(Y(\omega))));\mu]
  \;\le\; I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finer conditioning increases conditional mutual information when coarse carries no extra info]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_comp_conditioning_le_of_condMutualInfo_eq_zero}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $W : \Omega \to V$ and $f : V \to U$.  If $I[X : W \mid f \circ W;\mu] = 0$ (i.e., the
coarse variable $f \circ W$ carries all the information about $X$ that $W$ does), then
\[
  I[X : Y \mid f \circ W;\mu] \;\le\; I[X : Y \mid W;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Chain rule: splitting a left-side pair]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_prod_left_eq_add}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
For measurable $X$, $W$, $Y$, $Z$ with finite ranges under a zero-or-probability measure,
\[
  I[(X,W) : Y \mid Z;\mu]
  \;=\; I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] \;+\; I[W : Y \mid (X, Z);\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Chain rule: splitting a right-side pair]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_prod_right_eq_add}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_prod_left_eq_add}
\difficulty{3}
For measurable $X$, $Y$, $W$, $Z$ with finite ranges under a zero-or-probability measure,
\[
  I[X : (Y, W) \mid Z;\mu]
  \;=\; I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] \;+\; I[X : W \mid (Y, Z);\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Pairing the right variable cannot decrease conditional mutual information]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_le_prod_right_snd}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For measurable $X$, $Y$, $W$, $Z$ with finite ranges under a probability measure,
\[
  I[X : W \mid Z;\mu] \;\le\; I[X : (Y, W) \mid Z;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Strict prefix of a boolean vector]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.boolVectorStrictPrefix}
\leanok
For a boolean-vector-valued random variable $X : \Omega \to (\mathrm{Fin}\,m \to \mathrm{Bool})$
and an index $i : \mathrm{Fin}\,m$, the \emph{strict prefix} $\mathrm{boolVectorStrictPrefix}\,X\,i\,\omega$
is the restriction of $X(\omega)$ to coordinates $0, 1, \ldots, i-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Chain rule for conditional mutual information against a boolean vector]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_boolVector_eq_sum_strictPrefix}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.boolVectorStrictPrefix, ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_const_left, ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_prod_left_eq_add}
\difficulty{7}
For a boolean-vector-valued $X : \Omega \to (\mathrm{Fin}\,m \to \mathrm{Bool})$,
\[
  I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu]
  \;=\; \sum_{i=0}^{m-1}
        I[X_i : Y \mid (\mathrm{boolVectorStrictPrefix}\,X\,i,\, Z);\mu],
\]
where $X_i(\omega) = X(\omega)(i)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Iterated conditioning on a subset]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.cond_cond_eq_cond_of_subset}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For a finite measure $\mu$ and measurable sets $F \subseteq A$,
\[
  (\mu[\,|\,A])[\,|\,F] \;=\; \mu[\,|\,F].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Real-mass reweighting for nested conditioning events]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.measureReal_mul_cond_real_eq_measureReal_of_subset}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For a finite measure $\mu$ and measurable sets $F \subseteq A$,
\[
  \mu_{\mathbb{R}}(A) \cdot (\mu[\,|\,A])_{\mathbb{R}}(F) \;=\; \mu_{\mathbb{R}}(F).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional mutual information as an average over a finite partition]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_prod_conditioning_eq_sum}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.measureReal_mul_cond_real_eq_measureReal_of_subset}
\difficulty{6}
If the conditioning variable is a pair $(K, Z)$ with $K$ taking values in a finite type $A$,
then
\[
  I[X : Y \mid (K, Z);\mu]
  \;=\; \sum_{k : A} \mu_{\mathbb{R}}(K^{-1}\{k\}) \cdot I[X : Y \mid Z;\,\mu[\,|\,K \leftarrow k]].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional mutual information on an event is bounded by the unconditional value]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.measureReal_mul_cond_condMutualInfo_le_condMutualInfo_of_event_eq_preimage}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.cond_cond_eq_cond_of_subset, ProbabilityTheory.measureReal_mul_cond_real_eq_measureReal_of_subset}
\difficulty{7}
Let $A = Z^{-1}(B)$ for some measurable $B$.  Then, under a probability measure $\mu$,
\[
  \mu_{\mathbb{R}}(A) \cdot I[X : Y \mid Z;\,\mu[\,|\,A]]
  \;\le\; I[X : Y \mid Z;\,\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Chain rule for mutual information: splitting a right-side pair]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.mutualInfo_prod_right_eq_add}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
For measurable $X$, $Y$, $W$ with finite ranges under a zero-or-probability measure,
\[
  I[X : (Y, W);\mu] \;=\; I[X : Y;\mu] \;+\; I[X : W \mid Y;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional mutual information bounded by unconditioned mutual information]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_le_mutualInfo_of_condDependence_le}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.mutualInfo_comp_right_of_injective, ProbabilityTheory.mutualInfo_prod_right_eq_add}
\difficulty{5}
If $I[X : W \mid Y;\mu] \le I[X : W;\mu]$, then
\[
  I[X : Y \mid W;\mu] \;\le\; I[X : Y;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional entropy invariant under a.e.\ substitution]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condEntropy_congr_ae}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Under a probability measure, if $X =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} X'$ and $Y =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} Y'$
(with all four variables measurable and of finite range), then
$H[X \mid Y;\mu] = H[X' \mid Y';\mu]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional mutual information invariant under a.e.\ substitution of both variables]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_congr_ae_left_right}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.condEntropy_congr_ae}
\difficulty{4}
Under a probability measure, if $X =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} X'$ and $Y =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} Y'$,
then $I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] = I[X' : Y' \mid Z;\mu]$ (the conditioning variable $Z$ is
unchanged).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional mutual information invariant under a.e.\ substitution of all three variables]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_congr_ae}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.condEntropy_congr_ae}
\difficulty{4}
Under a probability measure, if $X =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} X'$, $Y =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} Y'$,
and $Z =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} Z'$, then $I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] = I[X' : Y' \mid Z';\mu]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-space a.e.\ congruence for conditional mutual information]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_congr_ae_finite}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.FiniteMeasureSpace, ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_congr_ae}
\difficulty{2}
Version of \lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_congr_ae} for finite measurable sample
spaces: measurability and finite-range conditions are inferred automatically from the
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.FiniteMeasureSpace} and \texttt{Finite} instances, so only
the a.e.\ equality hypotheses need to be supplied.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional mutual information determined by the joint law]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib.condMutualInfo_eq}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
If $(X, Y, Z)$ and $(X', Y', Z')$ have the same joint distribution (i.e., are identically
distributed), then $I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] = I[X' : Y' \mid Z';\mu']$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-space version: conditional mutual information determined by the joint law]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib.condMutualInfo_eq_finite}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.FiniteMeasureSpace, ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib.condMutualInfo_eq}
\difficulty{2}
Finite-space version of \lean{ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib.condMutualInfo_eq}: measurability
and finite-range conditions are inferred from \lean{CommunicationComplexity.FiniteMeasureSpace}
and \texttt{Finite} instances.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional mutual information invariant under injective recodings of right and conditioning variables]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.condMutualInfo_comp_right_conditioning_of_injective}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
If $f : T \to V$ and $g : U \to W$ are measurable injections, then
\[
  I[X : f \circ Y \mid g \circ Z;\mu] \;=\; I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Identical distribution of pairs preserved under conditioning on the same set]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib.cond_of_pair}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
If $(X, Y)$ and $(X', Y')$ have the same joint law and $s \subseteq B$ is measurable, then
$X$ under $\mu[\,|\,Y^{-1}(s)]$ and $X'$ under $\mu'[\,|\,Y'^{-1}(s)]$ are identically
distributed.
\end{theorem}
